title: Blocking the Event Loop in Node.js

scenes.line1: What happens if the event loop stalls?
scenes.say: Ever wondered what happens when Node's event loop gets stuck? Can your server still handle requests?

scenes.label: Blocking
scenes.sub: Synchronous code can freeze the event loop, stopping all other events.
scenes.say: Blocking means synchronous code runs so long that the event loop can't process anything else. Everything grinds to a halt.
For example, an infinite loop like this will totally freeze your server. No requests get handled until it's stopped.
To catch blocking code, I profile latency with clinic.js, check active requests, and watch for slow response times.

scenes.question: How do you block the event loop?
scenes.right: By running heavy synchronous code, like infinite loops or big computations.
scenes.say: Interviewers love this: How do you block the event loop? It's not about async code—it's about heavy synchronous stuff.
